correctness.rationale: For each d>0, the real orthogonal basis {1,cos(dt)-sinc d,sin(dt)} in averaged L²([-1,1]) yields the exact positive Gram formula L_d(x)=1+(cos(dx)-sinc d)²/A_d+sin²(dx)/B_d, A_d=(1+sinc(2d))/2-sinc² d, B_d=(1-sinc(2d))/2. Expanding convergent even analytic series in q=d² gives L_d(x)=9/4(5y²-2y+1)-3P(y)q/280+Q(y)q²/78400+O(q³), y=x², P=175y³-115y²+9y-5 and Q=11025y⁴-12180y³-1530y²+2028y+145. P is negative on [0,1/2] and strictly increasing on [1/2,1], has a unique zero y0≈0.645997059498281; x0=sqrt(y0)≈0.803739422635397. Exact polynomial identity Q=(63y-141/5)P-4/5(6675y²-3246y-5) makes Q(y0)<0. Hence sign changes at x0, where quartic suppression is strict. The implicit-function theorem applied to derivative wrt q produces a unique positive local maximizer q*(y)∝(y0-y) with square-root d* onset; the second derivative is negative at the branch. Independent SymPy polynomial identity/root checks and 8 rational Taylor/96 Gram finite tests corroborate but do not supply analytic uniqueness.
